gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Synology DS925+'s '2× M.2 NVMe' slots can't hold a storage pool, which is where Immich wants its Postgres database, unless the SSD is Synology-verified. ChatGPT's recommended setup (a 500 GB NVMe for the database) therefore works out of the box on the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus but not on the DS925+ with an ordinary NVMe drive.
standout_why: I compared against the three pages ChatGPT cited from docs.immich.app (Requirements, FAQ and Backup and Restore) and the mobile-backup.md page on GitHub. The Requirements page says the database 'should ideally use local SSD storage, and never a network share of any kind' and gives 6 GB minimum / 8 GB recommended RAM. None of these pages mentions Synology, NAS models, M.2 slots or storage pools (I checked the Requirements and FAQ pages for this). No result connects 'SSD for the database' to the fact that each maker means something different by its M.2 slots: Synology allows pools only on verified SSDs, QNAP's slots are PCIe Gen3 x1, and UGREEN's are PCIe 4.0 and can hold storage. ChatGPT's answer also skipped the DS225+'s 6 GB RAM ceiling and Immich's QSV note for Jasper Lake chips.
decides: It backs the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus ($619.99 at UGREEN's NAS store today) as the box where the plain 'NVMe for the Immich database' advice works. It also changes how the DS925+ should be presented: on stock DSM its M.2 database pool needs a Synology-verified SSD, the 4 GB of RAM is below Immich's 6 GB minimum, and Synology lists no hardware transcoding engine. The DS925+ wins on DSM backup tools, not on running Immich. For 2-bay buyers the DS225+ tops out at 6 GB, exactly Immich's minimum and below the 8 GB recommendation, which argues for the DXP2800 or QNAP TS-264 instead.

findings.label: Immich RAM requirement
findings.value: Minimum 6 GB, recommended 8 GB; with 4 GB Immich runs only with machine learning disabled
findings.note: Quoted: 'RAM: Minimum 6GB, recommended 8GB.' and 'For systems with only 4GB of RAM, Immich can be run with machine learning features disabled.' This is the yardstick for every box's default and maximum RAM below.

findings.label: Where Immich's database must live
findings.value: Local SSD, never a network share
findings.note: Quoted: Postgres 'should ideally use local SSD storage, and never a network share of any kind'. On a NAS that means an SSD storage pool or volume, not an SSD cache, so whether the M.2 slots can hold a pool is what counts.

findings.label: M.2 slots: what they can be used for
findings.value: 2× M.2 2280 NVMe; storage pools only on Synology-verified SSDs
findings.note: Spec footnote: 'Creating M.2 storage pools requires the use of Synology-verified SSDs'. SSD cache 'can be enabled with select compatible SSD'. Footnote: our page says '2× M.2 (Synology SSDs for pools)'. That is correct, but it is the reason the plain advice to add a 500 GB NVMe for the database doesn't work on stock DSM with a third-party drive.

findings.label: CPU / RAM / transcoding
findings.value: AMD Ryzen V1500B; 4 GB DDR4 ECC (max 32 GB, 16 GB × 2); no hardware transcoding engine listed
findings.note: 4 GB is below Immich's 6 GB minimum. Immich's hardware transcoding page lists AMD only through VAAPI, and the V1500B has no integrated GPU per Synology's spec (no transcoding row value). Warranty 3 years, extendable to 5.

findings.label: RAM ceiling vs Immich
findings.value: 2 GB DDR4 default, 6 GB maximum (2 GB + 4 GB); no M.2 slots listed
findings.note: Fully upgraded, it reaches exactly Immich's 6 GB minimum and can never reach the 8 GB recommendation. With no M.2 slot, the database has to sit on a SATA bay. CPU Intel Celeron J4125, 3-year warranty.

findings.label: CPU / RAM / M.2 link
findings.value: Intel Celeron N5095 with Intel UHD Graphics; 8 GB (max 16 GB, 2× 8 GB); 2× M.2 2280 PCIe Gen 3 x1
findings.note: Footnote: 'NVMe slots' here means Gen3 x1, one lane, about a quarter of an x4 link. The spec page doesn't say whether the slots can hold a pool or a cache. Warranty 3 years (accessories 1 year).

findings.label: Immich Quick Sync caveat for Jasper Lake
findings.value: Jasper Lake and Elkhart Lake CPUs must use CQP constant-quality mode; 11th-gen and older may need Low-Power mode; VP9 needs 9th gen or newer
findings.note: This affects the N5105 (Asustor AS5402T) and likely the N5095 (QNAP TS-264/TS-464). 'Intel CPU, hardware transcoding' therefore needs a settings change on these chips. The same page: AMD only through VAAPI; Raspberry Pi not supported; Quick Sync not supported on WSL2.

findings.label: Immich machine-learning acceleration on NAS chips
findings.value: OpenVINO lists 'Intel GPUs such as Iris Xe and Arc'; integrated GPUs 'more likely to experience issues… especially for older processors or servers with low RAM'; RKNN only on RK3566/RK3568/RK3576/RK3588
